title: service-account delegation model + signed audit attestations + KMS envelope provenance
author: Jordan K. Mills
description:
Summary: Introduce a service-account delegation model for RBAC v2, append cryptographic audit attestations to outgoing audit events, and record KMS envelope provenance metadata for keys used in envelope encryption. Goal is to improve forensic traceability for cross-service actions, enable least-privilege delegation flows for platform services, and allow compliance teams to verify key provenance and attestation signatures when auditing data residency and key use. Motivation: Current audit logs lack a cryptographic proof tying an action to a delegated service-account chain and the specific KMS envelope used. This makes post‑incident investigations and compliance attestations for data residency harder. Changes in this PR are designed to be additive and opt-in behind feature flags, with migration steps for existing audit-forwarders. Checklist: - [x] RBAC v2: introduce new ServiceAccountDelegation and DelegationBinding primitives - [x] Audit: add audit.attestation.{algorithm,signature,signer_id} fields and signed-detached attestations for high-sensitivity routes - [x] KMS: record envelope_provenance.{key_id,region,wrap_algorithm,wrapped_key_id} in event metadata - [x] Console: UI flag to opt-in per-tenant for signed attestations (backend + minimal frontend flag) - [x] Migrator: backfill lightweight provenance for recent events (best-effort) - [x] Tests: unit + e2e for delegation decision flow and attestation validation - [x] Docs: updated security/compliance guide and audit schema docs Highlights / Files changed (high level): - pkg/auth/delegation.go: new delegation model and policy evaluator (core logic) - api/audit/v2/schema.proto: audit event schema additions for attestation and provenance - cmd/audit-forwarder/main.go: attach signed attestations (configurable signer) - internal/kms/envelope_provenance.go: helper to capture and persist provenance at encryption time - migrations/202411_backfill_envelope_provenance.sql: best-effort backfill for recent events - web/console/src/features/compliance/AttestationsToggle.tsx: feature flag toggle and small notice - tests/integration/delegation_attestation_test.go: integration flows - deploy/helm/values.security.yaml: new feature flags and KMS signer config

Commit summary (high-level): 1) Add ServiceAccountDelegation objects and API DSL + evaluator (Jordan) 2) Wire delegation check into auth middleware and token introspection (Luca) 3) Audit attestation schema + sign/attach implementation for the forwarder (Priya) 4) KMS envelope provenance capture and propagation (Evelyn) 5) Migration and backfill scripts + docs (Jordan)

Small illustrative snippet (delegation policy evaluator):

// simplified pseudocode inserted in description: if request.actor.type == "service_account" && delegation.exists(request.actor.delegated_by) && delegation.allow(request.action, resource) then allow with audit.trace = delegation.chain

CI / checks: - lint: pass - unit tests: pass (coverage maintained for modified packages) - integration tests: had one transient failure initially (auth middleware race on cache invalidation), fixed by adding a short jitter and cache lock; rerun green - e2e on staging: pass - security-scan: pass (no new high findings) - compliance-schema-validator: pass

Review thread (selected): - Priya Rao (2024-11-03): "Can we avoid coupling the attestation signer to a single KMS key? Would like to see a signer rotation plan and JWK discovery." -- Author (2024-11-04): "Added signer config in helm values and a signer-provider interface; rotation documented in docs/ops/signer-rotation.md." - Luca Moretti (2024-11-06): "Looks good; one nit: the delegation policy evaluator should short-circuit if the request is from an interactive user (avoid extra lookups)." -- Author (2024-11-07): "Good catch. Added a fast path and unit test." - Evelyn Tan (2024-11-08): "We should ensure envelope_provenance doesn't leak PII. Confirmed provenance fields are key identifiers and regions only; no plaintext keys stored." -- Author (2024-11-09): "Confirmed and added automated scrubber in forwarder before persistence. Added docs note." - Security review (2024-11-10): "APPROVED with comments: ensure attestation signature verification is optional on read paths to avoid perf regressions; require verification for export/forensic flows." -- Author (2024-11-11): "Added verification flag and defaulted to off for read paths. For forensic exports a CLI flag enforces verification."

Migration notes: - New audit schema is backward-compatible: unknown fields will be ignored by older consumers. - A best-effort backfill job (migrations/202411_backfill_envelope_provenance.sql) annotates recent events with provenance where logs exist; full provenance requires instrumented encrypt calls. - Operators should enable attestation signer in helm values.security.yaml and supply signer KMS key ARN or signer-provider endpoint. For highest assurance, enable attestation signing + verification during forensic exports.

Security considerations: - Attestations are detached signatures (RFC 7515 style); payloads are canonical JSON of event headers to reduce equivocation. - Signer private keys must be protected in KMS/HSM or an approved signer-provider. - Rotations are supported via signer-provider interface and the sponsorrotation doc. - Rate-limit attestation signing to prevent signer quotas being exhausted.

Backward-incompatibility: None to runtime callers. Audit schema expands with additive fields; feature gated for storage/forwarding.

Release notes: - security: Add support for service-account delegation RBAC primitives and cryptographic audit attestations to improve traceability (ENG-4122). - compliance: Record KMS envelope provenance on encryption events to help data residency audits.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals by Priya and Security, CI green. Post-merge: triggered rollout to canary tenants with attestation_enabled=false by default; ops ran backfill job on staging and then progressively enabled signing for compliance customers.
